faqs.q: The Emergency provisions of the Indian Constitution are contained in which Part?
The Emergency provisions of the Constitution end with which Article?
The President can declare a National Emergency even before the actual occurrence of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion if satisfied that there is:
Which Amendment Act empowered the President to issue separate proclamations of National Emergency on different grounds, even if one proclamation is already in operation?
faqs.e: This provision was added by the 38th Amendment Act of 1975.

faqs.q: A National Emergency declared on the ground of war or external aggression is known as:
A National Emergency declared on the ground of armed rebellion is known as:
Which Amendment Act enabled the President to limit the operation of a National Emergency to a specified part of India?
Which Amendment Act substituted the words "armed rebellion" for "internal disturbance" as a ground for National Emergency?
The National Emergency of 1975 was declared on which ground, no longer available under the current Constitution?
The President can proclaim a National Emergency only after receiving a written recommendation from:
Which Amendment Act made it mandatory for the President to receive a written Cabinet recommendation before proclaiming a National Emergency?
faqs.e: This safeguard was introduced to eliminate the possibility of the Prime Minister alone taking such a decision, following the 1975 precedent where Indira Gandhi advised the President without cabinet consultation.

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act made the declaration of a National Emergency immune from judicial review?
Which Amendment Act deleted the provision making National Emergency declarations immune from judicial review?
In which case did the Supreme Court hold that a proclamation of National Emergency can be challenged on the ground of malafide or being based on wholly extraneous facts?
faqs.e: Minerva Mills vs. Union of India (1980).

faqs.q: A proclamation of National Emergency must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within:
Originally, the period allowed for parliamentary approval of a National Emergency proclamation was:
faqs.e: This was reduced from two months to one month by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.

faqs.q: Once approved by Parliament, a National Emergency continues for a period of:
A National Emergency, once approved, can be extended indefinitely with parliamentary approval renewed every:
A resolution approving the proclamation or continuance of a National Emergency must be passed by:
faqs.e: This requires a majority of the total membership of the House and a majority of not less than two-thirds of members present and voting.

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act introduced the special majority requirement for approving a National Emergency, which was previously passed by simple majority?
What fraction of the total membership of the Lok Sabha must give written notice to seek a special sitting for considering disapproval of a continuing National Emergency?
A special sitting of the Lok Sabha to consider a resolution disapproving continuation of a National Emergency must be held within:

Consider the following statements regarding a resolution disapproving the continuation of a National Emergency, as distinguished from a resolution approving its continuation:
(I) The disapproval resolution is required to be passed by the Lok Sabha only
(II) The disapproval resolution needs to be adopted by a special majority
(III) The continuance resolution needs to be passed by both Houses of Parliament
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: The disapproval resolution requires only a simple majority and only the Lok Sabha's approval; the continuance resolution requires a special majority and both Houses.

faqs.q: During a National Emergency, the executive power of the Centre extends to directing a state on:
faqs.e: In normal times the Centre can direct states only on certain specified matters; during a National Emergency this restriction is removed.

faqs.q: During a National Emergency, the Parliament becomes empowered to make laws on subjects mentioned in which List?
Laws made by Parliament on state subjects during a National Emergency become inoperative how long after the emergency ceases to operate?
During a National Emergency, the President can issue ordinances on state subjects if:

options.c: The Parliament is not in session

faqs.a: The Parliament is not in session

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act extended the executive and legislative consequences of a National Emergency to states not directly under the Emergency?
During a National Emergency, the President can modify the constitutional distribution of revenues between the Centre and states. Such modification continues till:

options.b: The end of the financial year in which the emergency ceases

faqs.a: The end of the financial year in which the emergency ceases

faqs.q: During a National Emergency, the life of the Lok Sabha may be extended by Parliament by law for a period of:
The extended life of the Lok Sabha during a National Emergency cannot continue beyond how long after the emergency has ceased to operate?
The term of which Lok Sabha was extended twice by one year at a time during the 1975 National Emergency?
Article 358 deals with the suspension of Fundamental Rights guaranteed under which Article?
Under Article 358, the six Fundamental Rights under Article 19 are suspended:

options.a: Automatically upon proclamation of National Emergency
options.c: Only by a separate Presidential order

faqs.a: Automatically upon proclamation of National Emergency

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act restricted Article 358 to apply only when the National Emergency is declared on the ground of war or external aggression, and not armed rebellion?
Article 359 authorises the President to suspend which of the following during a National Emergency?

options.a: The right to move any court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights
options.c: The powers of the Supreme Court

faqs.a: The right to move any court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights
faqs.e: Under Article 359, the Fundamental Rights as such are not suspended, only their enforcement; the rights remain theoretically alive.

faqs.q: Which two Articles guaranteeing Fundamental Rights are excluded from suspension of enforcement under Article 359, as per the 44th Amendment Act?

Consider the following statements regarding Articles 358 and 359:
(I) Article 358 is confined to Fundamental Rights under Article 19 only
(II) Article 359 automatically suspends Fundamental Rights as soon as the emergency is declared
(III) Article 358 operates only in case of External Emergency
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: Article 359 does not automatically suspend any Fundamental Right; it only empowers the President to suspend enforcement of specified rights via a Presidential Order.

faqs.q: Which of the following statements about Articles 358 and 359 is correct?

options.a: Article 358 extends to the entire country, while Article 359 may extend to the entire country or a part of it
options.b: Article 358 extends to a part of the country only, while Article 359 always extends to the whole country
options.c: Both Articles may extend to a part of the country only
options.d: Both Articles always extend to the entire country

faqs.a: Article 358 extends to the entire country, while Article 359 may extend to the entire country or a part of it

faqs.q: A Presidential Order suspending enforcement of Fundamental Rights under Article 359 must be laid before:
Which of the following is a similarity between Article 358 and Article 359?

options.a: Both require a separate Presidential order for suspension
options.b: Both provide immunity only to laws related to the Emergency, not other laws
options.d: Both apply only during Internal Emergency

faqs.a: Both provide immunity only to laws related to the Emergency, not other laws

faqs.q: How many times has a National Emergency been proclaimed in India so far?
The first proclamation of National Emergency was issued in which year?
faqs.e: It was issued in October 1962 on account of Chinese aggression in the NEFA (now Arunachal Pradesh) and remained in force till January 1968.

faqs.q: The first National Emergency, proclaimed in 1962, remained in force till which year?
Why was a fresh proclamation of National Emergency not needed at the time of the 1965 war with Pakistan?

options.b: The 1962 Emergency was still in operation
options.d: The President refused to sign it

faqs.a: The 1962 Emergency was still in operation

faqs.q: The second proclamation of National Emergency, made in December 1971, was issued in the wake of attack by:
The third proclamation of National Emergency was made in which year?
Both the second (1971) and third (1975) proclamations of National Emergency were revoked in:
The first two proclamations of National Emergency (1962 and 1971) were made on which ground?
Which commission was appointed after 1977 to investigate the circumstances warranting the 1975 National Emergency?
faqs.e: The Shah Commission did not justify the declaration, leading to the 44th Amendment Act of 1978 introducing safeguards against misuse.

faqs.q: Article 355 imposes a duty on the Centre to protect every state against external aggression and internal disturbance, and to ensure the state government functions in accordance with:
President's Rule can be proclaimed under Article 356 on grounds mentioned in Article 356 itself and also on a ground mentioned in which other Article?
Under Article 356, the President can proclaim President's Rule if satisfied that a situation has arisen, acting on:

options.a: A report of the Governor only
options.b: A recommendation of the Election Commission only
options.c: A resolution of the state legislature only
options.d: A report of the Governor or otherwise

faqs.a: A report of the Governor or otherwise

faqs.q: A proclamation imposing President's Rule must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within:
Once approved by Parliament, President's Rule initially continues for a period of:
President's Rule can be extended, with parliamentary approval every six months, for a maximum period of:
A resolution approving the proclamation of President's Rule or its continuation is passed by:
Which Amendment Act introduced restraint on extending President's Rule beyond one year, subject to two specified conditions?

Consider the following conditions that must both be fulfilled for extending President's Rule beyond one year:
(I) A National Emergency must be in operation in the whole of India or the whole/part of the state
(II) The Election Commission must certify that elections cannot be held due to difficulties
(III) The state High Court must approve the extension
Which of the above is/are among the conditions specified?
Which state's President's Rule was extended to a maximum period of five years under the 68th Amendment Act of 1991?
A proclamation of President's Rule may be revoked by the President at any time by a subsequent proclamation. Such revocation requires:
When President's Rule is imposed in a state, the President can take up the functions of the state government and powers vested in the:

options.d: Governor or any other executive authority

faqs.a: Governor or any other executive authority

faqs.q: When President's Rule is imposed, the President can declare that the powers of the state legislature are to be exercised by:
During President's Rule, the constitutional position, status, powers and functions of which body remain unaffected?
faqs.e: The President cannot assume the powers vested in the state High Court or suspend constitutional provisions relating to it.

faqs.q: When President's Rule is imposed, who dismisses the state council of ministers headed by the Chief Minister?
During President's Rule, the state administration is carried on, on behalf of the President, by:
Under President's Rule, when the state legislature is suspended or dissolved, the Parliament can delegate the power to make laws for the state to:

options.a: The President or any other authority specified by him/her

faqs.a: The President or any other authority specified by him/her

faqs.q: Laws made for a state by the Parliament or President during President's Rule continue to be operative even after President's Rule ends. This means such laws are:

options.b: Not coterminous with the duration of the proclamation
options.c: Valid only for six months after revocation
options.d: Automatically repealed when President's Rule ends

faqs.a: Not coterminous with the duration of the proclamation
faqs.e: Such laws can be repealed, altered, or re-enacted by the state legislature once restored.

faqs.q: Since 1950, President's Rule has been imposed on more than how many occasions?
President's Rule was imposed for the first time, in 1951, in which state?
After the 1977 Lok Sabha elections, the Morarji Desai government imposed President's Rule in nine Congress-ruled states on the ground that:

options.a: The states failed to implement central directions
options.b: The assemblies no longer represented the wishes of the electorate

faqs.a: The assemblies no longer represented the wishes of the electorate

faqs.q: In 1992, President's Rule was imposed in three BJP-ruled states on the ground that they failed to sincerely implement a Central ban on:
faqs.e: The three states were Madhya Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, and Rajasthan.

faqs.q: In which landmark case did the Supreme Court uphold the 1992 imposition of President's Rule on the ground that secularism is a "basic feature" of the Constitution?
faqs.e: S.R. Bommai vs. Union of India (1994).

faqs.q: The Supreme Court in the Bommai case did NOT uphold the validity of President's Rule imposed in which of the following?
faqs.e: The Court also did not uphold President's Rule in Karnataka (1989) and Meghalaya (1991).

faqs.q: The Bommai case propositions on Article 356 were based on the report of which commission?
faqs.e: Report of the Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State Relations (1988).

faqs.q: As per the Bommai case, the burden lies on which party to prove that relevant material exists to justify imposition of President's Rule?
As per the Bommai case, the state legislative assembly should be dissolved only after:

options.a: The Parliament has approved the presidential proclamation
options.b: The Election Commission certifies elections cannot be held

faqs.a: The Parliament has approved the presidential proclamation
faqs.e: Until such approval, the President can only suspend the assembly; if Parliament fails to approve, the assembly gets reactivated.

faqs.q: Which of the following statements regarding imposition of President's Rule, as per the Bommai case propositions, is correct?

options.a: The court can go into the correctness and adequacy of the material used by the President
options.b: The presidential proclamation imposing President's Rule is subject to judicial review
options.c: A new party at the Centre has authority to dismiss ministries formed by other parties in states
options.d: The satisfaction of the President can never be challenged under any circumstances

faqs.a: The presidential proclamation imposing President's Rule is subject to judicial review

faqs.q: Which of the following, as per the Bommai case (based on the Sarkaria Commission report), is considered a proper ground for imposing President's Rule?

options.b: Massive electoral defeat of the ruling party in Lok Sabha polls
options.d: Intra-party problems of the ruling party

faqs.q:
Consider the following situations regarding imposition of President's Rule:
(I) Internal subversion where a government is deliberately acting against the Constitution
(II) Physical breakdown where the government wilfully refuses to discharge constitutional obligations
(III) Internal disturbances not amounting to internal subversion or physical breakdown
Which of the above is/are considered a proper ground for imposing President's Rule?
faqs.e: Statement III is explicitly listed as an improper ground for imposing President's Rule.

faqs.q: Which of the following is a correct point of distinction between National Emergency and President's Rule?

options.a: National Emergency affects only the state under emergency, while President's Rule affects all states
options.b: National Emergency has no maximum prescribed period, while President's Rule has a maximum of three years
options.c: Both require approval only by simple majority
options.d: Both have a maximum prescribed period of three years

faqs.a: National Emergency has no maximum prescribed period, while President's Rule has a maximum of three years
faqs.e: National Emergency can continue indefinitely with parliamentary approval every six months, whereas President's Rule must end after a maximum of three years and normal constitutional machinery must be restored. See table below for the full comparison.

rows: Continue functioning; Centre gets concurrent powers
Parliament cannot delegate; must legislate itself
Parliament can delegate to President or specified authority
Lok Sabha can pass resolution for revocation
No such provision; only President can revoke

faqs.q: Article 360 empowers the President to proclaim a Financial Emergency if satisfied that a situation has arisen threatening:

options.c: The financial stability or credit of India

faqs.a: The financial stability or credit of India

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act made the President's satisfaction in declaring a Financial Emergency final, conclusive, and not questionable in any court?
Which Amendment Act deleted the provision making the President's satisfaction in declaring a Financial Emergency immune from judicial review?
A proclamation declaring Financial Emergency must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within:
Once approved by Parliament, a Financial Emergency continues:

options.a: For a maximum of three years

faqs.q: A resolution approving the proclamation of Financial Emergency is passed by:
A proclamation of Financial Emergency may be revoked by the President at any time by a subsequent proclamation. Such revocation requires:
During a Financial Emergency, the President may issue directions for the reduction of salaries and allowances of which of the following?

options.a: Only the Prime Minister and Cabinet
options.d: Persons serving the Union and judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts

faqs.a: Persons serving the Union and judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts

faqs.q: During a Financial Emergency, directions to a state may include a requirement to reserve which category of bills for the President's consideration after being passed by the state legislature?

options.d: Money bills or other financial bills

faqs.a: Money bills or other financial bills

faqs.q: Has a Financial Emergency ever been declared in India?
faqs.e: No Financial Emergency has been declared so far, though there was a financial crisis in 1991.

faqs.q: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar stated that Article 360 more or less follows the pattern of which US legislation?
Which member of the Constituent Assembly stated that the financial emergency provisions pose a serious threat to the financial autonomy of the states?
Which member of the Constituent Assembly described the Emergency provisions as "a chapter of reaction and retrogression"?
Which member of the Constituent Assembly feared the Emergency provisions would allow "a form of constitutional dictatorship"?
Which member of the Constituent Assembly, defending the Emergency provisions, labelled them "the very life-breath of the Constitution"?
Which member of the Constituent Assembly opined that the Emergency provisions would work as a "safety-valve" for maintaining the Constitution?
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, while defending the Emergency provisions, accepted that there was a possibility of the Articles being:

options.a: Abused or employed for political purposes

faqs.a: Abused or employed for political purposes

faqs.q:
Consider the following criticisms of the Emergency provisions raised in the Constituent Assembly:
(I) The federal character of the Constitution will be destroyed
(II) The financial autonomy of the states will be nullified
(III) The judiciary will be stripped of the power of judicial review permanently
Which of the above was/were actually raised as a criticism?
Article 353 of the Constitution deals with:

options.a: Duty of the Union to protect states

faqs.q: Which Article deals with the application of provisions relating to distribution of revenues while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation?
Which Article dealt with the application of the Emergency provisions to the state of Punjab and has since been repealed?
Which of the following correctly matches an Article with its subject matter?

options.a: Article 356 – Provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in states
options.b: Article 357 – Provisions as to Financial Emergency
options.c: Article 353 – Duty of the Union to protect states
options.d: Article 355 – Suspension of provisions of Article 19 during Emergencies

faqs.a: Article 356 – Provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in states
faqs.e: Article 357 deals with exercise of legislative powers under a proclamation issued under Article 356; Article 355 deals with the Union's duty to protect states; Article 353 deals with the effect of proclamation of Emergency. See table below for the complete Article-wise list.

rows: Duty of the Union to protect states against external aggression and internal disturbance
Provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in states
Exercise of legislative powers under proclamation issued under Article 356
Suspension of provisions of Article 19 during Emergencies
Suspension of enforcement of Part III rights during Emergencies
